## Claude

Here's where your Flutter packages live:

## Pub cache (shared across all Flutter/Dart projects)

**Location:** `C:\Users\aaa\AppData\Local\Pub\Cache` (~813 MB, 299 packages)

| Subfolder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `hosted\pub.dev\<pkg>-<version>\` | The actual unpacked package source for everything from pub.dev (e.g. `analyzer-6.4.1`, `riverpod-2.6.1`). This is where `flutter pub get` downloaded the 55 packages from your build log. |
| `hosted-hashes\` | Integrity hashes for each downloaded archive. |
| `_temp\` | Download staging area. |
| `active_roots` | Bookkeeping file listing projects that pin into the cache. |

`$PUB_CACHE` is **not set**, so Dart is using the Windows default (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Pub\Cache`). If you ever want it elsewhere (e.g. a non-system drive), set `PUB_CACHE` before running `flutter pub get`.

## Per-project files (in your repo)

- [flutter_app/pubspec.yaml](flutter_app/pubspec.yaml) — declared dependencies
- [flutter_app/pubspec.lock](flutter_app/pubspec.lock) — resolved versions (points into the cache above)
- `flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json` — generated by `pub get`, maps each package name to its absolute path in the cache. This is what the analyzer/build tools actually read.

## Useful operations

- **See where a specific package resolved to:** `flutter pub deps` (run inside `flutter_app/`)
- **Clean the cache for one project only:** delete `flutter_app/.dart_tool/` and re-run `flutter pub get` (cheap — re-resolves from cache, no re-download)
- **Nuke and re-download everything:** `flutter pub cache clean` (wipes the 813 MB above; next `pub get` re-fetches from pub.dev)
- **Same cache is also used by:** the Dart SDK directly, any other Flutter project on this machine, `dart pub global activate` tools

I need to be straight with you about the Windows situation. Let me first confirm Android actually builds:

**Android (`build_debug_android.bat`):** I ran `flutter build apk --debug` against your code — it succeeds. The APK builds in ~41s. So the **compile** is fine. If you're seeing an error, it's likely either: (a) `flutter run` choking on the emulator, (b) the app crashing at startup because the backend isn't up at `http://localhost:3000`, or (c) something device-specific. **I need the actual error text from your script run to fix it** — please paste what you saw.

**Windows (`build_debug_windows.bat`):** Confirmed failing. Root cause:

```
rive_common 0.4.15 → windows/CMakeLists.txt → set_target_properties(... VS_PLATFORM_TOOLSET ClangCL ...)
```

The plugin hardcodes the `ClangCL` MSBuild toolset, and your VS 2022 Enterprise install doesn't have the LLVM/Clang component. I tried overriding the toolset from your repo's `windows/CMakeLists.txt`, but rive_common *also* sets Clang-only `-Wno-*` flags globally (`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`), which MSVC rejects with `D8021`. So the plugin is genuinely Clang-only on Windows by design — you can't cleanly force it onto MSVC without a vendor-level patch.

My in-repo CMakeLists.txt change has been reverted (it didn't work cleanly).

### Two real fixes — pick one

**Option A — Install ClangCL in Visual Studio (recommended, durable)**

1. Open **Visual Studio Installer**
2. Click **Modify** on VS 2022 Enterprise
3. Go to **Individual components** tab → check:
   - `C++ Clang Compiler for Windows`
   - `MSBuild support for LLVM (clang-cl) toolset`
4. Install (~600 MB), then re-run `cmds\build_debug_windows.bat`

Keeps `rive` available for when real `.riv` assets ship. One-time, no code changes.

**Option B — Remove `rive` from the project**

`rive` is only used in [persona_avatar.dart](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/persona_avatar.dart#L52) and the file already has a gradient-circle fallback for when `riveAsset` is null (which it always is — you have no `.riv` assets yet). I'd:

- Remove `rive: ^0.13.13` from [pubspec.yaml](flutter_app/pubspec.yaml#L38)
- Strip the `rive.RiveAnimation.asset(...)` branch in `persona_avatar.dart`, keeping only the fallback

Cleaner than carrying an unused plugin. Easy to re-add when design ships actual Rive assets and you've installed ClangCL.

---

Which do you want? If you don't reply I'll go with **A** since it preserves your future option to use Rive. And paste the Android error text whenever you can — I can't fix what I can't see.

## Claude

Got it — Option A. The install is on your end since I can't drive the Visual Studio Installer. Let me give you the exact steps and the verification commands.

## Install ClangCL

1. Launch **Visual Studio Installer** (Start menu → "Visual Studio Installer")
2. Find **Visual Studio Enterprise 2022** in the list → click **Modify**
3. Switch to the **Individual components** tab
4. In the search box, type `clang` and check **both**:
   - ☑ `C++ Clang Compiler for Windows (xx.x.x)` — the actual clang-cl.exe
   - ☑ `MSBuild support for LLVM (clang-cl) toolset` — the MSBuild integration that recognizes `Platform Toolset = 'ClangCL'`
5. Click **Modify** (bottom right). ~600 MB download, ~5 min on a decent connection.

## When it's done, verify

Run this from a *fresh* shell (so PATH picks up the new toolchain):

```
cmds\build_debug_windows.bat
```

If it still fails on the `ClangCL` toolset error, run `cmds\build_windows.bat` (which does a non-interactive `flutter build windows --debug`) and paste the tail of the output — I'll dig in. Most likely cause of a residual failure: only one of the two checkboxes got installed.

While you do that, paste the Android error from `build_debug_android.bat` when you have a chance — the compile works on my end, so it's something the script does *after* the build.

- **`2cc959c`** — wire-up. `ConversationsService.sendMessage` now calls `ConversationOrchestrator.generateTutorReply` instead of the placeholder canned strings. `AiModule` is imported into `ConversationsModule`; `UserEntity` is added to fetch `current_level` / `native_language`. TypeScript compiles clean (`npx tsc --noEmit`).

## How to verify

1. Open LM Studio → load `openai/gpt-oss-20b` → Developer tab → **Start Server** (port 1234).
2. `cd backend && npm run start:dev`. Boot log should include `Using OpenAICompatibleProvider (label=lmstudio)`.
3. From the Flutter app: log in → pick a scenario → send a message. Reply should be an LM Studio response, not one of the three canned strings.
4. Sanity: stop LM Studio mid-session — next message still returns a (canned) fallback with a warning logged.

## What I deliberately didn't do

- **`scoreGrammar()` in `endSession()`** — §1.7 of the playbook flags structured-output as the risky bit for smaller local models. Smoke-test that with an explicit endpoint first per §1.7-1.8.
- **`json_object` fallback** in the provider's `structured()` method — only worth doing once you see `strict: true` actually fail with your loaded model.
- **Performance tuning** (§1.9) — `maxTokens=300`, `temperature=0.8` in the orchestrator. Tune after the first real run.

If `gpt-oss-20b` is too slow on CPU, the env will swap to a smaller model (`qwen2.5-7b-instruct`, `llama-3.1-8b-instruct`) with a one-line `AI_CHAT_MODEL=` edit.

## Claude

You don't have PostgreSQL or Docker installed yet. The project supports both paths — `npm run db:up` uses Docker; otherwise a native install works fine. Since you said "install PostgreSQL", I'll guide you through the native Windows install. Mentioning Docker only for completeness.

## Native install (recommended for your case)

### 1. Download

Grab the **PostgreSQL 16** installer for Windows x86-64 from EnterpriseDB:

https://www.enterprisedb.com/downloads/postgres-postgresql-downloads

(Pick `16.x` — your docker-compose pins `postgres:16-alpine`, so matching versions keeps migrations consistent.)

### 2. Run the installer

Choices that matter:

| Prompt | Value to use |
|---|---|
| Installation directory | Default (`C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16`) |
| Components | Keep all checked (PostgreSQL Server, pgAdmin 4, Stack Builder, Command Line Tools) |
| Data directory | Default |
| **Password for `postgres` superuser** | **`dev_password`** — must match `DB_PASSWORD` in [backend/.env](backend/.env) |
| Port | **`5432`** (default) |
| Locale | `[Default locale]` |
| Stack Builder | Skip (uncheck "Launch Stack Builder" at the end) |

Install takes ~3 min.

### 3. Create the `vlearn2` database

Two ways — pick one:

**Way A — pgAdmin (GUI):**
1. Open **pgAdmin 4** (just installed)
2. Set a master password for pgAdmin (any value — local-only)
3. Expand **Servers → PostgreSQL 16 → Databases**, enter `dev_password` when asked
4. Right-click **Databases → Create → Database…**
5. Name: `vlearn2` → Save

**Way B — psql (terminal):**
```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE vlearn2;"
```
(Enter `dev_password` when prompted.)

### 4. Verify the connection

From the backend folder:

```powershell
cd c:\project\vLearn2\backend
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -d vlearn2 -c "SELECT version();"
```

You should see something like `PostgreSQL 16.x on x86_64-windows…`.

### 5. Run migrations + seeds

```powershell
cd c:\project\vLearn2\backend
npm run db:migrate
npm run db:seed
```

`db:migrate` runs [src/database/migrations/1715800000000-initial-schema.ts](backend/src/database/migrations/1715800000000-initial-schema.ts) which creates the schema (`users`, `refresh_tokens`, `personas`, `scenarios`, `courses`, `conversation_sessions`, etc.) plus the `pgcrypto` extension. `db:seed` populates personas, scenarios, courses, achievements, and app config.

### 6. Start the backend

```powershell
cd c:\project\vLearn2\backend
npm run start:dev
```

Boot log should include the TypeORM connection success line and `Using OpenAICompatibleProvider (label=lmstudio)`. App is up on `http://localhost:3000`.

---

## Alternative — Docker (if you'd prefer)

If at any point you'd rather skip the native install: install **Docker Desktop for Windows**, then `npm run db:up` from `backend/` and the same migrations/seeds work. Faster to nuke and reset. ~5 GB install, needs WSL2.

---

## When you're done, tell me

Paste the output of:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -d vlearn2 -c "\dt"
```

after running migrations + seeds. I'll verify the schema looks right and we can move on to LM Studio smoke-testing.

If the installer asks something I didn't cover or the `db:migrate` step errors out, paste the error and I'll dig in.

## Claude

Confirmed:
- Backend IS running (port 3000 listening).
- The bug is in [app_router.dart](flutter_app/lib/core/router/app_router.dart): when auth resolves to `signedOut` while on splash, **none** of the redirect conditions match (splash is in `isPublic`), so `redirect` returns `null` → stuck.
- Secondary issue: the router uses `ref.watch(authProvider)` so it recreates the entire `GoRouter` on every auth change. That doesn't cleanly trigger a re-redirect on the *current* location — `refreshListenable` is the standard pattern.

Fixing both.

## Claude

Fixed and committed as `f7e80d6`.

**Two bugs, one file:**

1. `app_router.dart` redirect didn't have a case for `signedOut + splash` — splash was lumped into `isPublic`, so nothing redirected away from it after the auth check resolved. Added `if (!signedIn && loc == AppRoute.splash) return AppRoute.signIn;`.
2. The router used `ref.watch(authProvider)` which recreates the whole `GoRouter` on auth changes — that doesn't reliably re-run the redirect against the current location. Switched to the standard pattern: a single `GoRouter` with a `ChangeNotifier` bound to `refreshListenable`, bumped via `ref.listen`.

**Verify:** In the Flutter terminal hit **`R`** (capital R — hot restart, not hot reload, since the router provider changed shape). Splash should flash for ≤500ms then land on the Sign In screen.

If it does, you're good to register an account → onboard → start a conversation, which will exercise the full LM Studio → backend → Flutter path. If something hangs in that flow, share the symptom and I'll dig in.

## Claude

Most likely cause based on what I traced: **stale tokens in `flutter_secure_storage` from a previous backend run**, where the `refresh_tokens` row was wiped when you ran migrations against the fresh Postgres install. Your access token may have expired since you signed in earlier, and now the refresh attempt fails (DB has no matching row for the stored refresh token), so the interceptor surfaces the original 401.

Here's how to confirm and fix.

## Quick fix — hot-restart the Flutter app

In the terminal where `flutter run` is attached, hit **capital `R`** (hot restart, not lowercase `r` hot reload). On restart:

1. `_restore()` reads the cached access token, calls `/users/profile` → 401
2. `AuthInterceptor` tries `/auth/refresh` → also 401 (refresh row doesn't exist in DB anymore)
3. Interceptor clears storage → state goes to `signedOut`
4. The router fix from earlier sends you to `/signin`
5. Sign in (or sign up if you haven't yet) → fresh access + refresh, both stored, both valid in DB

After that, the Scenarios screen should load. If you don't have a user yet, sign up creates one.

## To confirm what's happening, check the backend terminal

When you trigger the failing request, the backend (`npm run start:dev`) should log one of:

- `JsonWebTokenError: invalid signature` → JWT secret mismatch (e.g., token was signed with an older secret)
- `TokenExpiredError: jwt expired` → access token aged past 15 min
- `UnauthorizedException: invalid_refresh` from the refresh call → refresh hash doesn't exist in the `refresh_tokens` table
- `relation "refresh_tokens" does not exist` → migrations didn't run

If you see one of those, that confirms the diagnosis. Paste whatever it actually shows and I'll narrow it down.

## Sanity check — verify the seed actually populated scenarios

While you're at it, in the backend terminal:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\PostgreSQL\16\bin\psql.exe" -U postgres -d vlearn2 -c "SELECT count(*) FROM scenarios WHERE status='published';"
```

Should be > 0 (the seed adds several published scenarios). If it's 0, run `npm run db:seed` from `backend/`.

If the count is fine and a fresh sign-in still 401s on scenarios, share the backend log line and I'll dig deeper.

## Claude

I have the full picture. Backend is fine — the bug is in the Flutter auth interceptor + auth state coordination. Two real latent bugs that match your symptom:

**Bug 1 — Silent token-clear:** when refresh fails, `AuthInterceptor` clears tokens from secure storage but never tells the auth provider. App keeps thinking it's signed in, router stays on `/home`, every subsequent request goes out **with no Authorization header → 401**, and the screen shows "Could not load…".

**Bug 2 — Concurrent-refresh starvation:** when home screen mounts it fires `/scenarios`, `/progress`, `/achievements` etc. in parallel. The first 401 sets `_refreshing = true` and tries to refresh. The others see `_refreshing == true` and just pass the 401 straight through without retrying. Even when refresh succeeds, those parallel requests already failed.

Fixing both, plus adding a force-sign-out path so a corrupted token state self-recovers.

## Claude

Committed as `9a49bae`.

## What was wrong

I confirmed via `curl` that the **backend is healthy** — a fresh sign-up returns a token that lets every protected endpoint (`/scenarios`, `/users/profile`, `/personas`, `/courses`, `/progress`, `/achievements`, `/conversations/sessions`) return 200. The bug was entirely in the Flutter auth interceptor:

1. **Silent token-clear** — on refresh failure, `AuthInterceptor` was clearing `tokenStore` but **never notifying `authProvider`**. The Riverpod state stayed `signedIn`, the router kept you on `/home`, every subsequent request went out with no Authorization header → 401 forever.
2. **Concurrent-refresh starvation** — `_refreshing: bool` meant only the *first* parallel 401 triggered a refresh; the others (`/scenarios` + `/progress` fire together on home mount) bypassed refresh and surfaced 401 to the screen.

## What I changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [auth_interceptor.dart](flutter_app/lib/core/api/interceptors/auth_interceptor.dart) | `_refreshing: bool` → `Completer<String?>` shared by all parallel 401s. New `onSessionInvalid` callback invoked on every refresh failure. `skipAuth` now short-circuits onError too. |
| [api_client.dart](flutter_app/lib/core/api/api_client.dart) | Wires `onSessionInvalid` to `authProvider.notifier.forceSignOut()`, microtask-deferred to avoid provider-graph re-entry. |
| [auth_provider.dart](flutter_app/lib/core/providers/auth_provider.dart) | New `forceSignOut()` — clears storage + sets state to `signedOut` (without calling the server, which would just 401 again). |

The router's `refreshListenable` (from the earlier splash fix) catches the state change and redirects to `/signin` automatically.

## Backend `Unauthorized` audit (per your request)

Every 401 surface, both sides:

**Backend** — all legitimate, none spurious:
- `auth/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts:23` — produces the generic `{"message":"Unauthorized"}` when JWT missing/invalid (the one you're seeing)
- `auth/auth.service.ts:80,98` — bad email/password on `/auth/signin`
- `auth/auth.service.ts:109,112` — bad/expired refresh token on `/auth/refresh`
- `admin/permissions/permission.guard.ts:33` — defensive throw, unreachable in practice
- `ai/providers/openai-compatible.provider.ts:111` + `anthropic.provider.ts:121` — wrap upstream AI API 401 (bad provider key); not user-facing

**Flutter** — three touchpoints, all in auth flow:
- `auth_interceptor.dart` — **the buggy one**, now fixed
- `error_interceptor.dart:55` — `isUnauthorized` getter on `ApiException` (defined but **no screen actually checks it** — only the raw `.toString()` shows up in error tiles)
- `auth_api.dart:23,35` — `skipAuth: true` on `/auth/signup` and `/auth/signin` so Bearer isn't attached. Correct.

## Verify

Hot restart (`R`) in the Flutter terminal. Three possibilities:
- **Stale tokens in storage** → splash → `_restore` 401 → refresh fails → `onSessionInvalid` → `/signin` automatically.
- **No tokens** → splash → `/signin` immediately.
- **Already valid tokens** → splash → `/home` or `/onboarding`. Scenarios load.

If you still see "Could not load" after a fresh sign-in, paste the **backend terminal output** for the failing request — it'll log the exact reason (`JsonWebTokenError`, `TokenExpiredError`, `auth.invalid_refresh`, etc.) and I can narrow further.

## Claude

Both builds green. Committed as `a0e1334`.

**Backend** — fixed [news.module.ts](backend/src/news/news.module.ts): `NewsStatus` is a pure type alias used in a `@Query()` decorator parameter, which under newer TS requires `import type` (not a value import). After the fix, `nest build` produces `backend/dist/` clean.

**Admin panel** — root cause was `cmds/build_admin.bat` running `npm ci`, which needs a `package-lock.json` that didn't exist in `admin_panel/`. First install silently no-op'd (harness reported exit 0 but actual log showed the lockfile-required error), so `next build` then failed with `'next' is not recognized`. Generated the lock file via `npm install` (434 deps) and committed it so `npm ci` works on fresh checkouts. `next build` produced `.next/` with all 7 routes prerendered (`/`, `/config`, `/news`, `/signin`, `/_not-found`).

**Not done** (flagging for separate tasks):
- 8 npm-audit findings on the admin panel (1 critical / 6 high / 1 moderate) — mostly Next 14.2.5 transitive dev deps. Bumping to Next 15 is its own task.
- `prompts/0517/thought.txt` is also modified in your working tree; left alone since it's unrelated.

Run `cmds\build_backend.bat` and `cmds\build_admin.bat` to verify; both should pass without intervention now.

## Claude

Implemented and committed as `9ee7623`. Both backend and admin panel build clean.

**What was wrong:** the previous spec had `POST /api/admin/auth/signup` as a *one-shot bootstrap* — first signup creates superadmin, then endpoint auto-closes with `admin.signup_closed`. The admin panel had no `/signup` page at all; the README pointed users to `curl`. That doesn't match your memory of "first → superadmin, rest → subadmin, signup stays open."

**What I changed:**

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [admin-auth.controller.ts](backend/src/admin/admins/admin-auth.controller.ts) | Removed the `ForbiddenException` branch. Role now picked from existing admin count: `adminCount === 0 ? 'superadmin' : 'admin'`. |
| [(auth)/signup/page.tsx](admin_panel/src/app/(auth)/signup/page.tsx) | **New page.** Mirrors `/signin`'s shadcn card layout. Zod schema matches the backend DTO (email, 2+ char display name, 12+ char password with lower/upper/digit). POSTs to `/admin/auth/signup`, stores tokens, redirects to `/`. |
| [(auth)/signin/page.tsx](admin_panel/src/app/(auth)/signin/page.tsx) | Added "No admin account yet? Sign up" link at the bottom. |
| [admin_panel/README.md](admin_panel/README.md) | Updated the bootstrap section to describe the new flow + a ⚠️ security note (this is permissive for dev; gate it before any public deploy). |

**Try it:** boot `cmds\start_backend.bat` + `cmds\start_admin.bat`, open `http://localhost:4000/signup`. Form submits → you land on `/` as superadmin (first time) or admin (subsequent).

**Security caveat I want to be explicit about:** open admin signup is a real liability if this panel ever ends up reachable from the public internet. The README and the controller docstring both flag this. If/when you deploy non-locally, pick one of: re-add auto-close, require invite codes, or IP-allow-list at the reverse proxy.

## Claude

Fixed and committed as `29727ed`.

**Root cause:** the admin signup controller went straight to `users.save()` without first checking whether the email already exists. When you signed up with the same email twice (or used an email that was already a Flutter user), Postgres' unique-constraint on `users.email` threw a `QueryFailedError` and Nest's default filter turned it into the generic `{"statusCode":500,"message":"Internal server error"}`.

**Fix:** added the same `findOne` + `ConflictException({ i18nKey: 'auth.email_taken' })` pre-check that `AuthService.signUp` uses for regular users. Verified with curl:
- First signup → 201
- Second signup with same email → 409 `{"i18nKey":"auth.email_taken"}`

The signup page already handles 409 (`"That email is already registered."`), so the UI message is correct end-to-end.

Backend was already running in watch mode so it picked up the change automatically. Try the signup again from the admin panel — duplicates will now show the clear error message instead of dying with a 500.

## Claude

This touches a lot — schema, entities, services, JWT, admin panel signin URL, and data migration. Let me run through the plan once briefly so you can redirect if it doesn't match your intent, then I'll execute.

**Plan:**

1. **New `admins` table** with the same shape as the admin-relevant slice of `users` (id, email unique, password_hash, display_name, role `'admin'|'superadmin'`, status, timestamps).
2. **New `admin_refresh_tokens` table** so admin sessions don't share `refresh_tokens` with users.
3. **Data migration** — copy existing admin/superadmin rows from `users` to `admins` (preserving UUIDs so `admin_permissions` and `admin_audit_log` entries still line up), then delete those rows from `users`.
4. **Drop FK constraints** that point to `users.id` from admin-touched tables (`admin_permissions`, `admin_audit_log`, plus `news.author_id`, `app_config.updated_by`, `uploaded_files.uploader_id` where admins can be the actor) — otherwise the delete in step 3 cascades or fails.
5. **New `AdminAuthService`** that operates on `admins` + `admin_refresh_tokens`. Mirrors the user-side `AuthService`. Admin endpoints (`/admin/auth/signup`, `/admin/auth/signin`, `/admin/auth/refresh`, `/admin/auth/signout`) all use it.
6. **JWT payload gets an `actor: 'user' | 'admin'` discriminator** so guards know which table the `sub` belongs to. The user-side JWT is unchanged behaviour-wise (defaults to `actor: 'user'`); admin tokens carry `actor: 'admin'`.
7. **Admin panel** — signin page calls `/admin/auth/signin` (currently calls `/auth/signin`); `api.ts` refresh hits `/admin/auth/refresh`.
8. **Flutter app** — no change. It only ever knew about `/auth/*`.

**What I'm deliberately *not* doing** in this pass: renaming the `user_id` column inside `admin_permissions` / `admin_audit_log` to `admin_id` (cosmetic, more code to chase), and building an "admins management" page in the panel. Both are good follow-ups.

Starting now. First the new entities + migration.

## Claude

Done. Committed in a single change with the migration + smoke tests.

## What's now in place

- **`admins` table** + **`admin_refresh_tokens`** — separate from `users` / `refresh_tokens`. `users.role` CHECK constraint tightened to `'user'` only, so the mix can't reappear.
- **Data migration** preserved UUIDs when copying admin/superadmin rows out of `users`, so existing `admin_permissions` and `admin_audit_log` rows still resolve to the right admin. Confirmed in DB: `thomas9123@atomicmail.io` (superadmin) and `hkc91123@outlook.com` (admin) are in `admins`; `users` has no admin rows.
- **`AdminAuthService`** — mirrors the user-side `AuthService` but operates on the admin tables, stamps every JWT with `"actor": "admin"`. User-side tokens now carry `"actor": "user"`.
- **Admin endpoints** — `/admin/auth/signup`, `/admin/auth/signin`, `/admin/auth/refresh`, `/admin/auth/signout` all go through the new service.
- **Admin panel** — signin page hits `/admin/auth/signin`, refresh helper hits `/admin/auth/refresh`.
- **Flutter app** — untouched. It only ever talked to `/auth/*` and `users`, both still work.

## Smoke test results (curl against the running backend)

```
admin signup            → HTTP 201, JWT payload: { role: 'admin', actor: 'admin', ... }
admin signin            → HTTP 200
admin refresh           → HTTP 200
user-side signin (admin email) → HTTP 401  ← correct, admins aren't in users
```

## What you need to do

1. **Restart your `cmds\start_backend.bat`** — your existing instance is stale.
2. Sign into the admin panel at `http://localhost:4000/signin` with `thomas9123@atomicmail.io`. The JWT will now show `"actor": "admin"`.
3. New admin signups (first → superadmin, rest → admin) are now driven by `COUNT(*) FROM admins`, completely independent of users.

## Deliberately deferred (separate tasks when you want them)

- Renaming `admin_permissions.user_id` → `admin_id` and same for `admin_audit_log` (cosmetic; data is already correct).
- An `actor_type` discriminator next to the dropped-FK columns (`news_posts.author_id`, `app_config.updated_by`, `uploaded_files.uploader_id`) so the DB can again enforce which table the actor belongs to.
- The admins-management page in the panel itself (the backend `/admin/admins` endpoints exist and now run against `admins`, but the UI is empty).

Committed as the head commit; story log in [story_claude/260518_0145_separate-admins-from-users-tables.md](story_claude/260518_0145_separate-admins-from-users-tables.md).

## What I changed

**Backend — new endpoint:**
- [`GET /admin/stats`](backend/src/admin/stats/admin-stats.controller.ts) returns `{users_total, users_active_30d, sessions_total, scenarios_published}`. Any admin/superadmin can read.

**Admin panel — five new pages so the sidebar stops 404'ing:**

| Route | What it does today |
|---|---|
| [`/admins`](admin_panel/src/app/(dashboard)/admins/page.tsx) | **Functional** — reads `/admin/admins`, lists sub-admins with status + permissions |
| [`/scenarios`](admin_panel/src/app/(dashboard)/scenarios/page.tsx) | **Functional read-only** — pulls from `/scenarios` (published only). Header notes drafts+CRUD need a future `/admin/scenarios` endpoint |
| [`/users`](admin_panel/src/app/(dashboard)/users/page.tsx) | Stub — flags missing `/admin/users` endpoint |
| [`/audit`](admin_panel/src/app/(dashboard)/audit/page.tsx) | Stub — `admin_audit_log` table exists but no read endpoint |
| [`/leaderboard`](admin_panel/src/app/(dashboard)/leaderboard/page.tsx) | Stub |

## ⚠️ Restart the backend

Your running backend is still on yesterday's code — that's why my live curl against `/admin/stats` returned 404 (the log on my temporary instance showed `EADDRINUSE :::3000`, confirming yours is still bound).

**Action:** stop your `cmds\start_backend.bat` window (Ctrl+C) and re-launch. After restart, the boot log should show `Mapped {/api/admin/stats, GET} route`. Then the dashboard will render four stat cards instead of the error message.

## What I deliberately didn't ship

- Per-row admin actions on `/admins` (suspend/restore/delete/grant) — backend endpoints already exist, the UI is the work.
- Admin-only scenarios endpoint with drafts + create/edit/publish.
- `/admin/users` (list+search+suspend), `/admin/audit` (paginated log read), `/admin/leaderboard` (top-N + export). The stub pages name each missing endpoint so they're obvious next-task candidates.

## Claude

Committed as `030ba1c`. Single-file change to [sign_in_screen.dart](flutter_app/lib/features/auth/sign_in_screen.dart) — no provider or signup changes.

## What you'll see

When sign-in fails, the new soft-green banner replaces the red one and shows one of:

| Error | Message shown to user |
|---|---|
| Bad email/password (401, `auth.invalid_credentials`) | **Email or password is not correct.** |
| Account suspended / forbidden (403) | This account can't sign in right now. Please contact support. |
| Network / timeout / DNS failure | Couldn't reach the server. Check your internet connection and try again. |
| Backend 5xx | Something went wrong on our side. Please try again in a moment. |
| Anything else | Sign in didn't work. Please try again. |

Colors: pale green bg with mint border in light mode, deep green-gray in dark mode, info icon instead of error icon.

## Debug-side

The full raw error still goes to your `flutter run` terminal and DevTools:
- `[sign_in] raw error: …` via `debugPrint`
- structured `developer.log` with tag `sign_in_screen` for filtering

Hot-restart the app to pick up the change. Try a wrong password and confirm the banner reads "Email or password is not correct." while your `flutter run` terminal still prints the full DioException.

| session_report | report load |
| settings | model-registry status tile |

Instead one of ~10 polite sentences based on what actually happened: `"Email or password is not correct."`, `"You need to sign in again."`, `"We couldn't find that. Full-page errors get a "Try again" button.

**Developer-visible** — every error path logs the raw exception with a screen tag to the `flutter run` terminal and DevTools (`developer.log` + `debugPrint`). Stripped in release.

## Claude

[backend/.env](backend/.env) — local, gitignored, this is the one the running backend actually reads. The LM Studio block looks like this (from earlier in the session):

```env
# ─── AI Provider — LM Studio (offline) ──────────────────────
AI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible
AI_CHAT_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b
AI_ANALYSIS_MODEL=openai/gpt-oss-20b
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://localhost:1234/v1
OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed
AI_PROVIDER_LABEL=lmstudio
```

Keys you'd typically tweak:

| Key | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `AI_PROVIDER` | `openai-compatible` (LM Studio / Ollama / Groq), `anthropic`, etc. |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | LM Studio defaults to `http://localhost:1234/v1`. Change if you bound it to a different port. |
| `AI_CHAT_MODEL` / `AI_ANALYSIS_MODEL` | Exact model id LM Studio shows in the Developer tab after loading. |
| `AI_PROVIDER_LABEL` | Cosmetic label printed in the backend boot log. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | LM Studio ignores it — keep `not-needed`. |

**[backend/.env.example](backend/.env.example)** is the tracked template — same keys, comments explain each. If you ever blow away `.env`, copy `.env.example → .env` and refill secrets.

**Restart required.** NestJS reads `.env` once at boot, so after any edit stop your `cmds\start_backend.bat` (Ctrl+C) and relaunch. The boot log will print `AI provider: openai-compatible` and `Using OpenAICompatibleProvider (label=lmstudio)` so you can verify it picked the new values up.

4. Errors and Fixes:
- **ClangCL missing (Windows build)**: `rive_common` needs ClangCL toolset. User chose to install via VS Installer.
- **l10n.yaml `synthetic-package` deprecation**: Removed the key.
- **Splash screen stuck**: Router had no case for `signedOut + splash`. Fixed by adding explicit redirect case.
- **401 stranding**: `AuthInterceptor` cleared tokens but didn't notify `authProvider`. Fixed with `onSessionInvalid` callback + `forceSignOut()`.
- **Concurrent 401**: Multiple requests returning 401 simultaneously → only first got refresh. Fixed with `Completer<String?>`.
- **Backend TS1272**: `NewsStatus` type alias used in decorator. Fixed with `import type`.
- **Admin signup 500 on duplicate email**: Controller didn't check for existing email. Fixed with `findOne` + `ConflictException`.
- **Admin panel tabs 404**: Pages didn't exist. Created stubs/functional pages for all tabs.

## Claude

Here's the process. There are **3 places** a migration name lives — all 3 must match or TypeORM will re-run or fail:

---

**1. The file name**
```
backend/src/database/migrations/1715800000000-initial-schema.ts
```

**2. The class name inside the file**
```ts
export class InitialSchema1715800000000 implements MigrationInterface {
```

**3. The row in the `migrations` table in PostgreSQL**
```
name = "InitialSchema1715800000000"
```

---

### Steps to rename one migration

1. Rename the `.ts` file to the new name
2. Change the class name inside the file to match

## Entity Summary

Here's the table name and FK relationship to `users` table for each entity:

| File | Table Name | FK Column to Users |
|------|------------|-------------------|
| **refresh-token.entity.ts** | `vl_refresh_tokens` | `user_id` |
| **conversation.entity.ts** | `vl_conversation_sessions` | `user_id` |
| **progress.entity.ts** | `vl_skill_snapshots` | `user_id` |
| | `vl_user_progress` | `user_id` |
| | `vl_user_scenario_completions` | `user_id` |
| **guard-violation.entity.ts** | `vl_guard_violations` | `user_id` |
| **achievement.entity.ts** | `vl_achievements` | (none - master data) |
| | `vl_user_achievements` | `user_id` |
| **scenario.entity.ts** | `vl_scenarios` | `author_id` |

All entities reference the users table via a `uuid` column. Most use `user_id` as the FK column, while `vl_scenarios` uses `author_id` to track which user created/authored the scenario. The `vl_achievements` table is master data with no direct user reference (users are linked through the `vl_user_achievements` join table).
```

## Claude

Two root causes fixed:

1. **Missing `INTERNET` permission** — Android apps must declare this explicitly; without it all network calls fail silently as a connection error.
2. **Cleartext blocked** — Android 9+ blocks `http://` by default. The new `network_security_config.xml` allows cleartext only to `10.0.2.2` (emulator host), `localhost`, and `127.0.0.1`. All other hosts still require HTTPS.

Do a full rebuild (`flutter run`) — hot-restart won't pick up manifest changes.

## Claude

Done. Here's what changed:

**`write()`** — serializes `AppConfig` to JSON then `base64Encode(utf8.encode(json))` before writing to disk.

**`loadOrInitialize()`** — reads the file then calls `_decodeContent()` which tries `base64Decode` first; if that throws (old plain-JSON file), it uses the raw string as-is. This means any existing config file on a user's device is read correctly on the first launch after the update, and silently re-written in base64 the next time the config is saved.

**Windows dev config** — already re-encoded to base64, ready for the next `flutter run`.

how can i change env if i use LLAMA_CPP for backend ai provider.  give me only instructions

## Claude

llama.cpp's `server` exposes an OpenAI-compatible API, so `AI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` stays. Only the endpoint + label change:

1. Start `llama-server` (typically on port 8080):
   ```
   llama-server -m models/your-model.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
   ```

2. Edit `backend/.env`:
   - `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://<host>:8080/v1` (e.g. `http://localhost:8080/v1`)
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY=not-needed` (llama.cpp ignores it)
   - `AI_CHAT_MODEL=<model-id-llama-reports>` — run `curl http://<host>:8080/v1/models` to see the exact id; many builds just answer to any string, so the existing value often works
   - `AI_ANALYSIS_MODEL=<same as above>`
   - `AI_PROVIDER_LABEL=llamacpp`

3. Leave `AI_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` unchanged.

4. Restart the backend (`npm run start:dev` or `pm2 restart vlfs-backend`).

Verify with: `curl -s http://<host>:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"<your-model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'` — if you get a JSON reply, the backend will too.

**Important note about why you're still seeing it in `/Android/data/...`:** that's the fallback path, used when writing to `/storage/emulated/0/...` fails. On Android 11+, the public-storage write needs **MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE** granted at runtime — the manifest entry alone isn't enough. The first launch opens the system Settings page where you must manually toggle **"Allow management of all files"** for this app. Until that toggle is on, the file will keep landing at `/Android/data/com.ryongma.vfls/files/룡마/가상외국어회화/app_config.json` (still the new subfolder layout, just the app-scoped root).

To verify: after granting the permission, delete the old fallback file and relaunch — you should see `/storage/emulated/0/룡마/가상외국어회화/app_config.json` created.

## Claude

Done. New behavior on Android:

1. **Check permission explicitly** — `Permission.manageExternalStorage.isGranted`
2. **If granted** → create `/storage/emulated/0/룡마/가상외국어회화/` if missing, then return `app_config.json` from there. If a fallback file exists from a previous run, copy it into the public path and delete it (no data loss).
3. **If not granted** → write to `<external-storage>/룡마/가상외국어회화/app_config.json` (app-scoped). On the next launch after you grant the permission in Settings, it'll auto-migrate to the public path.

**What you need to do on the device:**
1. `flutter run` to install the new build
2. App opens Settings → grant **"Allow management of all files"** to this app
3. Restart the app — the file will now live at `/storage/emulated/0/룡마/가상외국어회화/app_config.json`, and any earlier fallback file will be moved there automatically.

## Claude

Two changes:

1. **`main.dart`** — now requests **both** `Permission.storage` (legacy READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) and `Permission.manageExternalStorage`. Manifest entries alone don't grant runtime access on Android 6+; an explicit prompt is required.

2. **`app_config.dart`** — the gate for the public path now accepts **either** permission. So:
   - Android ≤ 12 → legacy storage grant is enough
   - Android 11+ → MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE works
   - Android 13+ → MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is effectively the only option

**To take effect:** `flutter run` to reinstall, then accept the standard storage prompt **and** toggle "Allow management of all files" on the Settings page that opens. After that the file should land at `/storage/emulated/0/룡마/가상외국어회화/app_config.json`, and any old fallback file gets migrated automatically.

## Claude

Done. To switch formats, edit one line in [`flutter_app/lib/core/config/app_config.dart`](flutter_app/lib/core/config/app_config.dart):

```dart
static const bool encodeAsBase64 = true;  // ← flip to false for plain JSON
```

- `true` → `write()` saves base64-encoded JSON
- `false` → `write()` saves human-readable JSON
- `loadOrInitialize()` already auto-detects either format via `_decodeContent()`, so flipping the flag won't break an existing config file — the next `write()` just re-saves in the new format.

## Claude

`dart:developer`'s `log()` writes to the Dart VM service — visible in Flutter DevTools "Logging" tab and `flutter run` terminal, but **not** in Android Logcat. Android Logcat only sees stdout, which is what `print()` / `debugPrint()` write to (under the `flutter` tag).

Two options:

**1. Switch to `debugPrint` (simplest, shows everywhere):**

```dart
import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

void logx(String tag, Object message) {
  debugPrint('[$tag] $message');
}
```

This shows in Logcat under tag `flutter` (filter `flutter` in Logcat) **and** in the `flutter run` terminal, IDE Run console, and DevTools.

**2. Keep `dart:developer` and view it in the right place:**

- Run `flutter run` and watch the terminal — `dev.log()` output appears there
- Or open Flutter DevTools → **Logging** tab — that's the canonical destination for `dev.log()`
- Or in Android Studio: the **"Run"** tool window (where the Flutter run output appears), not Logcat

**Why Logcat doesn't see it:** `dev.log()` is routed through `dart:developer` IPC to the Observatory/VM service. Only platform `Log.d/i/w/e` calls and stdout/stderr from the Dart side reach Android's logcat. The Flutter engine forwards `print`/`debugPrint` to stdout, hence Logcat.

If you change `logx` to use `debugPrint`, the message from line 53 will show up under tag `flutter` in Logcat — filter by `flutter` (or just `config_baseurl111`) to find it.

Swagger is mounted at the **`api/docs`** path (relative to the host root — `SwaggerModule.setup` ignores the global prefix). With `PORT=5100` from your `.env`:

- **Locally**: http://localhost:5100/api/docs
- **From your remote backend host** (the IP in `_defaultBackendHost`): http://172.86.121.43:5100/api/docs

The OpenAPI JSON spec itself is at the same path with `-json` appended, e.g. http://localhost:5100/api/docs-json.

A node process (PID 22340) is bound to port 5100 but no HTTP request to it completes — every probe times out. So the backend process is alive, but either still booting, hung mid-startup, or has crashed its handler without releasing the port.

**Next steps to unblock it:**

1. **Find the terminal running the backend.** The output should show whether it's still loading or has thrown an error. The last line should be something like:
   ```
   [Nest] LOG ... Nest application successfully started
   ```
   If you don't see that, it never finished bootstrapping.

2. **If it's stuck**, kill and restart:
   ```powershell
   Stop-Process -Id 22340 -Force
   cd c:\project\vLearn2\backend
   npm run start:dev
   ```
   Watch the console — Swagger registers itself near the end of bootstrap, so if it crashes earlier you won't see `/api/docs`.

3. **Likely culprit:** the AI provider URL in `.env`:
   ```

   ```
   If that host is unreachable from your dev machine, the NestJS `OnModuleInit` for the AI provider may hang on the initial probe. Try either bringing that endpoint back up, or temporarily point it at a no-op URL.

Once the backend logs `Nest application successfully started`, http://localhost:5100/api/docs will respond.

## Claude

Two processes listening on port 5100 — that's the problem. PID 18648 (the backend) listens on IPv6 `::` while **PID 14392** is also listening on IPv4 `127.0.0.1:5100` and has 3 stuck connections. `http://localhost:5100` resolves through IPv4 first on Windows, so it hits PID 14392 — which doesn't speak HTTP — and hangs.

## Claude

Found it — the conflict is **VS Code's port-forwarding feature** (PID 14392, `Code.exe`). VS Code auto-detected `PORT=5100` from the `.env` and grabbed `127.0.0.1:5100` for forwarding, intercepting requests before they reach the actual backend on IPv6.

**Fix in VS Code:**

1. Open the **Ports** panel — `View → Ports` (or `Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Ports: Focus on Ports View")
2. Find the row for port `5100`
3. Hover the row and click the trash/X icon, **or** right-click → **"Stop Forwarding Port"**
4. Reload — `http://localhost:5100/api/docs` should now hit the real backend

**Alternative:** disable auto-forwarding globally so this stops happening:

- `Ctrl+,` → settings
- Search "auto forward ports"
- Set **`Remote: Auto Forward Ports`** to `off` (or change `Remote: Auto Forward Ports Source` to a less aggressive mode)

After unforwarding, you can verify:

```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5100 -State Listen
```

Only the IPv6 `::` line owned by your node PID should remain. Then http://localhost:5100/api/docs will load.

## Claude

**Root cause: VS Code is hijacking both ports on `127.0.0.1`.**

| Port | IPv6 `::` listener | IPv4 `127.0.0.1` listener |
|------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| 5100 | PID 24156 — **node** (your backend) ✓ | PID 14392 — **Code.exe** (VS Code) ✗ |
| 4100 | PID 8840 — **node** (admin panel) ✓ | PID 14392 — **Code.exe** (VS Code) ✗ |

When you type `localhost:5100` in a browser, Windows resolves `localhost` to IPv4 (`127.0.0.1`) first → that hits **VS Code's port-forwarding listener**, which doesn't speak HTTP → request times out. The actual backend on the IPv6 wildcard never sees the traffic.

**Fix — stop VS Code from forwarding these ports.** Two options:

**Option A (one-time, per port):**
1. In VS Code: `View → Ports` (or `Ctrl+Shift+P` → **"Ports: Focus on Ports View"**)
2. Right-click row for **5100** → **"Stop Forwarding Port"**
3. Right-click row for **4100** → **"Stop Forwarding Port"**

**Option B (permanent):**
1. `Ctrl+,` → settings
2. Search **"auto forward ports"**
3. Set `Remote: Auto Forward Ports` to **off**, then reload VS Code

After either fix, both URLs will work:
- http://localhost:5100/api/docs
- http://localhost:4100/

Verify with this one-liner — only the `::` row should remain for each port:

```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5100,4100 -State Listen | Select LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
```

Quick guide to adding a free Rive avatar — the rendering code at [tutor_avatar.dart:179](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_avatar.dart#L179) is already correct, you just need to drop a `.riv` file in the right folder and point the persona row at it.

---

### 1. Where to get free `.riv` files

| Source | Why |
|---|---|
| **rive.app/community** | Official gallery — filter "Free" or "Remix". Look for "character", "avatar", "face". Examples: *"Login Machine"* (the bear), *"Idle Character"*, *"Animated Login Screen"*. Click → **Download `.riv`**. |
| **rive.app/marketplace** | Some free ones marked "Free". |
| **github.com/rive-app/rive-flutter/tree/main/example/assets** | Official sample `.riv` files you can use directly (e.g. `off_road_car.riv`, `little_machine.riv`). |

Pick something with **idle / talking / listening** state machine triggers if you want the mood-driven animation to work. If you just want a static character, any avatar will do.

---

### 2. Drop it into the project

Save the file at:

```
flutter_app/assets/animations/persona_leo.riv
```

Use a `persona_<slug>.riv` filename so it matches the backend's `rive_asset` column (e.g. for Leo → `persona_leo.riv`).

The folder is already declared in `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` under `assets:` → `assets/animations/`, so Flutter will pick it up. No `pubspec` edit needed.

Run:
```
flutter clean
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

---

### 3. Tell the backend to use it

Set the persona's `rive_asset` column in the `vl_personas` table. Two ways:

**Option A — Admin panel** (recommended): edit the persona, set `rive_asset = persona_leo.riv`, save.

**Option B — SQL:**
```sql
UPDATE vl_personas SET rive_asset = 'persona_leo.riv' WHERE slug = 'leo';
```

---

### 4. Heads-up about the path inconsistency I mentioned

The two widgets handle the `rive_asset` value differently today:

- [tutor_avatar.dart:179](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_avatar.dart#L179) builds the path as `'assets/animations/$asset'` → expects `rive_asset = 'persona_leo.riv'`
- [persona_avatar.dart:67](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/persona_avatar.dart#L67) uses `riveAsset!` raw → expects `rive_asset = 'assets/animations/persona_leo.riv'`

I'd recommend storing the **short form** (`persona_leo.riv`) in the DB and fixing `persona_avatar.dart` to prepend the folder. Want me to do that fix now so both widgets behave the same way?

---

### 5. (Optional) Hooking state machine inputs

If your downloaded `.riv` has a state machine with inputs like `talking`, `listening`, `idle`, you can drive them from `widget.mood`. Replace the bare `RiveAnimation.asset(...)` with a `StateMachineController`-backed widget — happy to write that wrapper if your `.riv` has inputs. Open the file at rive.app/play to see what state machines and inputs it exposes.

## Claude

Already done — both pieces are in place:

**Manifest declaration** ([android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:4](flutter_app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L4))
```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO"/>
```

**Runtime check** ([audio_recorder.dart:80](flutter_app/lib/core/speech/audio_recorder.dart#L80))
```dart
Future<bool> requestPermission() async {
  final status = await pp.Permission.microphone.request();
  ...
}
```

**Call site before recording** ([tutor_mode_view.dart:124](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_mode_view.dart#L124))
```dart
final granted = await recorder.requestPermission();
if (!granted) {
  ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar(
    const SnackBar(content: Text('Could not open the microphone.')),
  );
  return;
}
```

So the answer is **yes to both**, and **yes, both are already done**.

The rules in general:

| Layer | Why both are needed |
|---|---|
| Manifest `RECORD_AUDIO` | Tells Android the app *might* request mic access. Without it, the runtime request will be auto-denied. |
| Runtime `Permission.microphone.request()` | Android 6+ requires user consent at runtime even when the manifest declares the permission. First call shows the system dialog; subsequent calls return the cached status. |

The current code calls `request()` lazily (right when the user taps the mic button), which is the recommended pattern — not at app startup. The user sees the system dialog with context.

If you want to be extra polite, you can call `Permission.microphone.status` first to skip the dialog when it's already granted — but `.request()` already does that internally, so the current code is fine.

The system prompt for the tutor conversation is built in **[backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts](backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts)** — the `PromptBuilderService.buildSystemPrompt()` method at [line 11](backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts#L11).

It produces a single string from:
- `persona.name`, `persona.style`, `persona.specialties` (from `vl_personas`)
- `scenario` block — title, setting, tutor role, user role, objectives, key phrases (from `vl_scenarios`)
- `userLevel` (1–6 → A1–C2 label) and `userNativeLanguage` (from `vl_user_info`)
- A fixed 10-rule INSTRUCTIONS block

The full flow:

| Step | File:line | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Build | [prompt-builder.service.ts:11](backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts#L11) | `buildSystemPrompt(persona, scenario, userLevel, userNativeLanguage)` returns the string |
| 2. Orchestrate | [conversation.orchestrator.ts:28](backend/src/ai/conversation.orchestrator.ts#L28) | `generateTutorReply()` calls the builder, passes result to `ai.chat({ systemPrompt, ... })` |
| 3. Send | [openai-compatible.provider.ts:52](backend/src/ai/providers/openai-compatible.provider.ts#L52) | `{ role: 'system', content: req.systemPrompt }` is added to `messages[]` and forwarded to the model |

The orchestrator also reuses the same builder in [`suggestNextLine()`](backend/src/ai/conversation.orchestrator.ts#L106) (appends a "give one short sentence" instruction) and uses a different builder method `buildGrammarPrompt()` / `buildFeedbackPrompt()` for analysis flows ([prompt-builder.service.ts:49](backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts#L49) and [:65](backend/src/ai/prompt-builder.service.ts#L65)).

To **change what the tutor is told**, edit the template literal in `buildSystemPrompt()` (lines 26–46). To **change inputs** (e.g. include scenario difficulty, or `cid_username`), pass extra fields from `conversations.service.ts` `sendMessage()` where the orchestrator is called.

- **rive.app/community** → filter "Free". Search "character", "avatar", "face". Click one → top-right **Download** button → choose `.riv`.
- **GitHub rive-flutter examples**: https://github.com/rive-app/rive-flutter/tree/main/example/assets — files like `off_road_car.riv`, `little_machine.riv`, `vehicles.riv` work out of the box.
- **A safe simple test file**: https://cdn.rive.app/animations/vehicles.riv (download then save locally).

For a first test, just grab one of the GitHub example files — they're guaranteed to load.

---

### 2. Drop it into the Flutter project

Save it as:

```
flutter_app/assets/animations/persona_leo.riv
```

The folder is already declared in [pubspec.yaml](flutter_app/pubspec.yaml) under `assets:` → `assets/animations/`, so no pubspec edit is needed.

If you want a different filename, name it `persona_<slug>.riv` so it matches the persona's `slug` column in `vl_personas`.

---

### 3. Point the persona at it

The widget loads from `'assets/animations/$asset'` where `$asset` comes from `persona.riveAsset` ([tutor_avatar.dart:183](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_avatar.dart#L183)), which maps to the DB column `vl_personas.rive_asset`.

Set it via SQL (or the admin panel):

```sql
UPDATE vl_personas SET rive_asset = 'persona_leo.riv' WHERE slug = 'leo';
```

Store just the **filename** — the widget adds the `assets/animations/` prefix.

---

### 4. Fix a latent crash before you run

[tutor_avatar.dart:117](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_avatar.dart#L117) currently does `AppConfig.logx("assets path", asset!);` — the `!` will throw if any persona has `rive_asset = NULL`. Guard it:

```dart
if (asset != null) AppConfig.logx("assets path", asset);
```

Want me to make that edit now?

---

### 5. Run on Android

```
cd flutter_app
flutter clean
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

Open a conversation with the persona you updated. You should see the Rive animation playing inside the circle. Watch Logcat (filter `flutter`) — you'll see:

```
[assets for] Leo
[assets path] persona_leo.riv
```

If the asset can't load, the widget falls back to the `CartoonFace` ([tutor_avatar.dart:194](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_avatar.dart#L194))) — so no crash, but you'll know it didn't load.

---

### 6. (Optional) Drive Rive state-machine inputs from mood

If your `.riv` has a state machine with boolean / trigger inputs like `talking`, `listening`, `idle`, you can wire them to `widget.mood`. That needs a `StateMachineController` instead of the plain `RiveAnimation.asset`. Easiest way:

1. Open your `.riv` at https://rive.app/play, hit the **inspect** panel → note the **artboard name**, **state machine name**, and **input names**.
2. Tell me those three things and I'll swap the Rive widget for a controller-driven version that maps:
   - `TutorMood.idle` → idle input
   - `TutorMood.listening` → listening input
   - `TutorMood.speaking` → talking input

For a first run, skip step 6 — just confirm the avatar shows up at all, then iterate.

---

### Recap of what you need

|---|---|
| A `.riv` file | Download from rive.app/community or rive-flutter examples |
| Folder declared in pubspec | ✓ already done |
| Permission/runtime checks | ✓ irrelevant for asset bundle |
| Persona row pointing at file | Need to `UPDATE vl_personas.rive_asset` |
| Null-safety fix at line 117 | Open todo — say the word and I'll fix it |
| State machine integration | Optional, later |

Say "fix the null thing" when you're ready and I'll patch it.

## Claude

All three tasks complete. Summary:

**Task 01 — Prompt template editor** (largest, end-to-end feature)
- New `vl_prompt_templates` table (migration 1780300000000) seeded with the existing three prompts (`tutor_system`, `grammar`, `feedback`).
- `PromptBuilderService` rewritten to render `{{group.field}}` placeholders from the active DB row, with built-in fallbacks if the row is missing.
- New `/admin/prompt-templates` CRUD endpoints (`config.edit` permission).
- New admin **Prompts** tab with one editor card per template, click-to-append placeholder chips, and live save.

**Task 02 — Admin panel audit**
- Root cause across 3 form pages: the local `Field` helper was a plain function component, swallowing react-hook-form's `ref`. Converted to `forwardRef` in `personas/[id]`, `personas/new`, `scenarios/new`.
- Scenarios list had a link to a non-existent `/scenarios/[id]` route → demoted the title to plain text.
- Documented the type-drift on nullable email and the placeholder `/audit` page.

**Task 03 — Edit tutor pre-fill**
- Same root cause as the audit findings — the missing ref prevented `reset()` from writing API data into the inputs.
- Fixed by the Task 02 forwardRef conversion.

**Verification**: backend `tsc` clean, admin panel `tsc` clean, migration applied, unit tests `2/2` passing.

## Claude

Here's how to actually test it on Android.

---

## Where TTS lives in this app

| Piece | File |
|---|---|
| Engine wrapper | [flutter_app/lib/core/speech/sherpa_onnx_tts.dart](flutter_app/lib/core/speech/sherpa_onnx_tts.dart) |
| Call site | [tutor_mode_view.dart:113](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_mode_view.dart#L113) — `tts.speak(...)` on the latest assistant message |
| Model bundle root | `getExternalStorageDirectory()` on Android → `/Android/data/com.ryongma.vfls/files/models` |
| Manifest | `<modelRoot>/manifest.json` |

## What TTS needs to work

Three preconditions, in order:

1. **Model bundle present on the device.** `manifest.json` + the `tts/model`, `tts/tokens`, and `tts/espeak-ng-data/*` files it lists must all exist under `<modelRoot>` and their SHA-256s must match.
2. **`ttsService.isAvailable == true`.** Set in `initialize()` only after the sherpa-onnx native engine constructs successfully ([sherpa_onnx_tts.dart:113](flutter_app/lib/core/speech/sherpa_onnx_tts.dart#L113)).
3. **A persona with a valid `voice_id`** — or any voice in `manifest.tts.voices` to use as fallback.

If any one fails, the app falls back silently (`catchError` at [tutor_mode_view.dart:113](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_mode_view.dart#L113)) and the avatar just doesn't speak.

---

## Three-step test on Android

### Step 1 — Confirm the model bundle is on the device

```
adb shell ls -la /sdcard/Android/data/com.ryongma.vfls/files/models
adb shell cat /sdcard/Android/data/com.ryongma.vfls/files/models/manifest.json
```

You should see `manifest.json` plus `tts/model.onnx` (or `.onnx.q4` etc.), `tts/tokens.txt`, and `tts/espeak-ng-data/...`. If the folder is missing or empty, the launcher will route you to the **"Models not installed"** screen on next start — there's nothing to test until you drop a bundle in.

### Step 2 — Watch Logcat while you open a conversation

```
adb logcat -v color | grep -i -E "flutter|tts|sherpa"
```

Look for these in order:
- `TTS: OfflineTts ready with N voices.` ← native init succeeded
- or `TTS: model registry not ready (...)` ← bundle not installed
- or `TTS: native init failed` ← model files corrupt / wrong format

### Step 3 — Trigger speech from the UI

1. Sign in → pick or create a conversation → switch to **Tutor mode** (the face icon)
2. Send any message → the assistant reply triggers `tts.speak(last.content, voiceId: persona.voice_id)` ([tutor_mode_view.dart:113](flutter_app/lib/features/conversation/widgets/tutor_mode_view.dart#L113))
3. You should hear audio and the avatar should pulse (the `isSpeakingStream` drives the breathing/scale animation in `tutor_avatar.dart`)

---

## Quick diagnostic helper (optional)

If you want a one-button check that doesn't depend on the conversation flow, add a temporary debug button on the Settings screen that calls `ttsService.speak('hello, this is a test', voiceId: ...)` directly. Say the word and I'll wire it up — useful for verifying TTS without going through the AI / orchestrator.

---

## Common failure modes — quick lookup

| Symptom | Most likely cause |
|---|---|
| App routes to **"Models not installed"** screen | `manifest.json` missing under `/Android/data/.../files/models/` |
| Logcat says `model registry not ready` | manifest present but some listed file failed hash/size verify |
| Logcat says `TTS: native init failed` | wrong sherpa-onnx model variant or missing `espeak-ng-data/` dir |
| Tutor avatar shows the reply text but no sound | `isAvailable` is true but persona `voice_id` doesn't match any entry in `manifest.tts.voices` — falls through to `sid = 0`; if voices list is empty, throws and `catchError` swallows |
| Audio plays once, then silence on repeats | not a bug — second hit returns cached WAV from `<appSupport>/cache/tts/<sha>.wav`. Delete that folder to force resynthesis. |

Run those three steps and paste back what Logcat shows. I can pinpoint the failure from there.

what is the rebuild command for flutter

## Claude

Two flavors depending on what you mean by "rebuild":

```
flutter run                      # build + install + attach (Dart hot-reload ready)
flutter clean && flutter run     # full clean rebuild — use after manifest / native / pubspec changes
```

For a release APK without installing:
```
flutter build apk --release
```

Quick reference — when each is needed:

| You changed... | Command |
|---|---|
| Dart code only | press `r` in the run console (hot reload) or `R` (hot restart) |
| `pubspec.yaml` | `flutter pub get` then `flutter run` |
| `AndroidManifest.xml`, `build.gradle`, `*.kt`/`*.java`, `res/` (icons!) | `flutter run` — the native build runs automatically |
| Something looks stuck after the above | `flutter clean && flutter run` |
| You want a shippable APK | `flutter build apk --release` (output: `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-release.apk`) |

Useful flags:
- `flutter run -d <device-id>` — pick a specific device (`flutter devices` to list)
- `flutter run --release` — release-mode debug build
- `flutter run -v` — verbose (helps when a build fails silently)

For your case (you just swapped launcher icons in `mipmap-*`), the Android resources picker reruns automatically — `flutter run` is enough; no need for `flutter clean` unless the old icon caches in the launcher (rare).

## Claude

The model file `sum-small-IQ1_S.gguf` is broken under LM Studio's bundled llama.cpp build. Two things are wrong:

## The error

```
error loading model: error loading model vocabulary: invalid unordered_map<K, T> key
```

This is llama.cpp blowing up while parsing the GGUF tokenizer block. Two causes are common, both apply here:

1. **`IQ1_S` is a bleeding-edge 1.5-bit quant** (the log says `1.5625 bpw`). IQ1 quants have historically broken in older LM Studio builds because of how the vocab is packed.
2. **The model was likely quantized with a newer llama.cpp than your LM Studio ships with** — the vocab schema added fields that the older loader doesn't understand, so its `unordered_map` lookup fails.

So it's not your config — it's the model file vs. the runtime.

## What to do

Pick one (in order of effort):

| Option | Effort | Result |
|---|---|---|
| **Use a different quant of the same model** — grab `Q4_K_M` or `Q5_K_M` from `bartowski/sum-small-GGUF` instead of `IQ1_S` | tiny | almost certainly works, much better quality (Q4_K_M ≈ 4 bpw) |
| **Use a different model entirely** — your previous `.env` had `AI_CHAT_MODEL=Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf` which was working. Revert and load that in LM Studio. | tiny | known-good baseline |
| **Update LM Studio** to the latest version (it bundles a newer llama.cpp build that fixes most IQ1/vocab edge cases) | small | might unblock IQ1_S — but Q4 is still a better tradeoff |

## My recommendation

Don't use `IQ1_S`. At 1.5 bpw the model will be noticeably worse than `Q4_K_M` (~4 bpw) for almost the same RAM footprint, and that quant is a regular source of vocab/loader bugs. Also `sum-small` is a 4B Phi-3 — for your English-tutor use case `Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf` (your previous choice) or `Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` will give clearly better replies and load reliably.

## Quick fix in your stack

1. In LM Studio, **Discover → Downloads**: grab `bartowski/sum-small-GGUF` at `Q4_K_M` (or just re-enable your existing Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M).
2. Start it from LM Studio's **Developer** tab so it listens on `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1`.
3. Update `backend/.env`:
   ```
   AI_CHAT_MODEL=<exact id LM Studio shows in /v1/models>
   AI_ANALYSIS_MODEL=<same>
   ```
   Verify with `curl http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models`.
4. Restart the backend.

That should get the tutor reply pipeline talking again. Once it's responding, you can experiment with smaller quants — just stay at Q3_K_M or higher; below that, "weird tokenizer errors" and "the model speaks gibberish" are the two most common outcomes.

## Claude

The actual error is buried near the top of all that Gradle noise:

```
C:\project\vLearn2\flutter_app\.dart_tool\package_config.json does not exist.
Did you run this command from the same directory as your pubspec.yaml file?
Target dart_build failed
Target gen_dart_plugin_registrant failed
```

That file is generated by `flutter pub get`. It was either never created, deleted by a `flutter clean`, or wiped by something else. Without it Flutter can't resolve any package, so the Android build fails before it even tries to compile Dart.

## Fix

From the Flutter project root:

```
cd c:\project\vLearn2\flutter_app
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

That single `flutter pub get` recreates `.dart_tool/package_config.json` + `.dart_tool/version` + the `pubspec.lock` if missing.

If `flutter pub get` itself errors, run it with `-v` and check the output:

```
flutter pub get -v
```

## Common reasons it disappears

| Cause | Tell |
|---|---|
| Just ran `flutter clean` | `.dart_tool/` is gone entirely → `flutter pub get` |
| Switched Flutter SDK versions | `.dart_tool/` was created by another SDK and got invalidated → `flutter pub get` |
| `pubspec.yaml` edit + IDE didn't auto-fetch | IDE may rely on a save-action that didn't fire → `flutter pub get` |
| `pubspec.yaml` has an actual error (bad dep, version conflict) | `flutter pub get` will report it explicitly — fix and re-run |

## Sanity check after

```
dir .dart_tool\package_config.json     # should now exist
flutter doctor                          # confirm SDK is healthy
flutter run                             # rebuild
```

Once `flutter pub get` succeeds, the Gradle build will get past `:app:compileFlutterBuildDebug` cleanly.

what is the git command to see available branch

## Claude

```
git branch          # local branches only — current one has a *
git branch -a       # local + remote-tracking
git branch -r       # remote-tracking only
git branch -vv      # local + upstream tracking + last commit
```

Most useful in practice: `git branch -vv` (you see which local branch tracks which remote and the latest commit on each).

what is git amend command?

## Claude

`git commit --amend` rewrites the most recent commit. Two common uses:

```
git commit --amend                       # edit the message of HEAD
git commit --amend --no-edit             # add staged changes to HEAD, keep message
git commit --amend -m "new message"      # replace message in one shot
```

Typical flow when you forgot a file:
```
git add forgotten_file.ts
git commit --amend --no-edit
```

## Important caveats

- **Amend rewrites history.** The amended commit has a new SHA. If the previous commit was already pushed, a normal `git push` will be rejected — you'd need `git push --force-with-lease`, which can stomp on teammates' work on a shared branch. Don't amend pushed commits unless you're sure no one else has based work on them.
- **Amend = new commit, old one is orphaned.** Reflog (`git reflog`) keeps it findable for a while if you need to recover.
- **Only amends HEAD.** To edit an older commit, use `git rebase -i <commit>^` and mark the target as `edit` or `reword`.

## When NOT to amend
- After hook failure during commit — the previous commit is still HEAD, so amending modifies *that* one. The convention in this repo (and most others) is to fix the issue, re-stage, and create a **new** commit instead.
- On already-pushed commits on a shared branch.

how to download github release

## Claude

To download a GitHub release, you have a few options:

## Via Browser
1. Go to the repo: `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`
2. Click **Releases** (right sidebar) or visit `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases`
3. Under the release you want, expand **Assets** and click the file to download

## Via `gh` CLI
```powershell
# Latest release, all assets
gh release download --repo <owner>/<repo>

# Specific tag
gh release download v1.2.3 --repo <owner>/<repo>

# Just one asset by pattern
gh release download v1.2.3 --repo <owner>/<repo> --pattern "*.zip"

# Download to a specific folder
gh release download v1.2.3 --repo <owner>/<repo> --dir C:\downloads
```

## Via `curl` / direct URL
Asset URLs follow this pattern:
```
https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset-filename>
```

```powershell
curl -L -o file.zip https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/download/v1.2.3/file.zip
```

For **private repos**, add an auth header:
```powershell
curl -L -H "Authorization: token $env:GITHUB_TOKEN" -o file.zip <url>
```

## Via PowerShell
```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/download/v1.2.3/file.zip" -OutFile file.zip
```

## "Latest" shortcut
GitHub provides a redirect for the latest release:
```
https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download/<asset-filename>
```
This always points to the newest release's asset — useful in scripts.

## Claude

That release page has source archives and signature files. Here are the direct download commands:

## Source tarball (most common)
```powershell
# .tar.bz2 (smallest)
curl -L -o mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2 https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls/releases/download/mbedtls-3.6.2/mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2

# .zip (Windows-friendly)
curl -L -o mbedtls-3.6.2.zip https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls/archive/refs/tags/mbedtls-3.6.2.zip
```

## Via `gh` CLI (downloads all assets)
```powershell
gh release download mbedtls-3.6.2 --repo Mbed-TLS/mbedtls
```

## Via PowerShell native
```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest `
  -Uri "https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls/releases/download/mbedtls-3.6.2/mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2" `
  -OutFile mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2
```

## Verify signature (optional)
The release also publishes a `.asc` GPG signature:
```powershell
curl -L -o mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2.asc https://github.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls/releases/download/mbedtls-3.6.2/mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2.asc
gpg --verify mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2.asc mbedtls-3.6.2.tar.bz2
```

## Claude

Fixed. The root cause: `sherpa_onnx` package (^1.10.46) guards every native constructor with a "bindings initialized?" check, and `initBindings()` was never called.

**Change:** [flutter_app/lib/main.dart](flutter_app/lib/main.dart) — call `sherpa_onnx.initBindings()` once at startup right after `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()`. Both STT and TTS now share the same FFI setup, so the first `speak()` no longer crashes.

Rebuild and try TTS again:
```powershell
flutter run
```

Reading the output:

**What's actionable now**
- `record` 6.2.0 → 6.2.1 — safe patch (no pubspec.yaml edit needed). `flutter pub upgrade` will pick it up along with a few transitive bumps (`code_assets`, `hooks`, `objective_c`, etc.).
- Everything else marked `*` under "Upgradable" stays the same because your pubspec.yaml constraints hold them down.

**What "Resolvable" means**
The "Resolvable" column shows what you could get *if* you loosen `pubspec.yaml`. Big bumps available:
- `flutter_riverpod` 2.6 → 3.x (breaking — Riverpod 3 reworked APIs)

**Discontinued packages**
`js`, `build_resolvers`, `build_runner_core` are all **transitive** (not in your pubspec.yaml). They'll disappear when their parent packages (build_runner, etc.) drop them. Not your problem to fix.

**Suggestion**
Run `flutter pub upgrade` for the safe patches now. Don't touch the majors (Riverpod 3, go_router 17, Rive 0.14) unless you have time for breakage — each one needs a focused migration.

## Claude

Good news — the logic is **already cross-platform**. `ModelRegistry.resolveModelRoot()` takes the path from `app_config.json` and calls `Directory(path).existsSync()` / `_hasSherpaLayout()` without any Android-specific code. Windows accepts forward slashes too.

The problem is a typo in your Windows JSON: you wrote `"models"` (plural), but the code reads `"model"` (singular).

Two ways to fix this:

1. **Quick fix:** rename `"models"` → `"model"` in [app_config.json](flutter_app/build/windows/x64/runner/Debug/app_config.json).
2. **Robust fix:** accept both keys in the code so the typo never bites again. I'll do this — `"models"` is a natural-sounding key for a folder of model files.

**One thing to double-check** — your override path `C:/Users/aaa/Downloads/VLearn2/VLearn2/sherpa_2023` needs this layout for the registry to accept it:

```
sherpa_2023/
  stt/
    *.onnx          ← at least one .onnx file
    tokens.*        ← at least one tokens file
  tts/              ← (optional, but expected for TTS)
  vad/              ← (optional, but expected for VAD)
```

If the layout is right, on next launch you'll see in the console:
```
[model-registry] using app_config.json model override → C:/Users/aaa/Downloads/VLearn2/VLearn2/sherpa_2023
```

If the layout is wrong, you'll see:
```
[model-registry] model override path "..." missing or has no expected layout — falling back to unpacked .dat
```

Run with `flutter run -d windows` and check the console — the `[model-registry]` line tells you which path won.

## Claude

That `RangeError 0..1: 2` is the Rive runtime tripping over something while wiring up state-machine inputs or applying values. Without a stack trace I can't pinpoint the exact line — but the cause is almost always the same: `tutor_hiro.riv` was exported from a newer Rive editor than your pinned `rive: ^0.13.20` runtime knows how to walk. The top-level `RiveFile.import` in our usable-check passes, but a deeper read during artboard/state-machine attachment trips.

Two layers of fix:

**(1) Defensive guards so this never crashes the conversation screen** — wrap `_onRiveInit` and the mood writes so any internal Rive throw degrades to the CartoonFace fallback instead of a red error.

## Claude

Done — the conversation screen should no longer surface that RangeError. Two changes:

1. **Most likely root cause fixed:** `TutorMood.disappointed` was setting `emotion = 2`, but your `tutor_hiro.riv` only defines emotion states `0` and `1` — the runtime range-checks that array and throws. Clamped to `1` until you ship a real "sad" viseme.

2. **Defensive nets:** `_onRiveInit` and `_applyMoodToRive` are now wrapped in try/catch. If the newer Rive editor ever exports another field the pinned `rive: ^0.13.20` can't parse, the avatar degrades to the default timeline (or CartoonFace) instead of throwing a Flutter framework error.

**If you still see the error after this:**
Tell me the full stack trace next time. The most likely follow-up fix is to bump `rive` to `0.14.7` (I warned earlier this is a breaking-major upgrade — affects `RiveAnimation`, `StateMachineController`, and input APIs). Until then, also try re-exporting `tutor_hiro.riv` from the Rive editor with **File → Export → Runtime Version** set to an older release.

## Claude

I have enough to migrate. The Rive 0.14 API is significantly different:

- `RiveAnimation.asset(path, onInit:)` → `RiveWidgetBuilder(fileLoader:, builder:, onLoaded:)`
- `StateMachineController.fromArtboard(...).findInput<T>(name)` → `stateMachine.trigger(name)` / `.boolean(name)` / `.number(name)`
- `SMITrigger`/`SMIBool`/`SMINumber` → `TriggerInput`/`BooleanInput`/`NumberInput`
- Requires one-time `RiveNative.init()` at app startup (similar to sherpa-onnx)

Let me migrate. First, the init call.

**To filter in Android Studio Logcat:**
- Tag: `flutter`, search: `[stt]` — STT only
- Tag: `flutter`, search: `[tts]` — TTS only
- Tag: `flutter`, search: `stt\|tts` — both (regex)

**What each line tells you:**
- `mic.stop -> 0 bytes` → recorder isn't producing audio (mic permission or driver issue).
- `engine.transcribe flavour=none` → no recognizer was built (model files missing from manifest).
- `engine.result = ""` → recognizer ran but heard silence/noise.
- `aborted — speech models not ready` → `ModelRegistry.snapshot()` says the bundle isn't installed (check `[model-registry]` line).

## Claude

Yes — `debugPrint` writes to the Flutter process's stdout. But the catch is **where that stdout goes depends on how you launched the app.** Looking at your screenshot:

- **`flutter logs`** (your terminal command) only shows output from a *separately-running* Flutter process attached to a connected device. On Windows desktop it usually shows nothing — `flutter logs` is really an Android-attached-device tool. That's why your `Select-String "stt"` returned blank.

- **You have the right file open already.** The tab in your IDE — `extension-output-Dart-Code.dart-code-#3-flutter` — IS the place. That's the VSCode Dart Code extension's log channel, and it's where every `debugPrint` lands when you run the app from VSCode/Cursor.

So the three real places `[stt]` / `[tts]` lines will appear, depending on how you started the app:

| How you launched | Where the logs go |
|---|---|
| **F5 / "Run" in VSCode/Cursor** | Bottom panel → **DEBUG CONSOLE** tab (visible in your screenshot), AND the `extension-output-Dart-Code.dart-code-#3-flutter` file you already have open |
| **`flutter run -d windows` in a terminal** | That same terminal's stdout |
| **`flutter run -d <android-id>` and want to grep separately** | Then `flutter logs` works (Android only) |

Good — the pipeline is working end-to-end and we can see exactly where it fails. The recognizer **ran** (348 ms) but returned `""`. That almost always means one of three things:

1. The PCM buffer is silent (mic isn't actually capturing).
2. The PCM buffer has audio but the **format doesn't match what sherpa-onnx expects** (it needs mono, 16-bit, little-endian, **16 kHz**).
3. Sample-rate mismatch — recorder produces 44.1/48 kHz but `transcribe` hard-codes `sampleRate = 16000`, garbling timing.

The math is consistent: 114498 bytes ÷ 32000 B/s (16 kHz × 2 bytes) = 3.58 s, which matches the wall-clock duration. So the recorder really is producing the format it claims. That rules out format mismatch — leaving two suspects:
